protocol.stream: same deterministic synthetic public feature/action/outcome sequence for each learner

findings.interpretation: On this single synthetic stream MR32 uses 10.6% more serialized bytes and 66% more deep Python object bytes than the conventional prototype; peak traced allocation is about 32% higher. Wall time was about 4.1-4.6x higher. The memoryless predictor has much smaller serialized/object state, but its traced transient peak is not the lowest due to Python allocation behavior. The prototype has no demonstrated resource advantage.

limitations: Single fixed 256-step synthetic stream; no randomization or task-level efficacy.
Windows and Ubuntu hosted runners are not calibrated hardware, and wall time is noisy.
tracemalloc is not process RSS; Python deep-size is implementation/interpreter-dependent.
MR32 checkpoint envelope differs from controls' state serialization formats; canonical equivalent persistence format is needed.
No reward, transfer, prediction accuracy or decision improvement measured.
decision: NEGATIVE FOR RESOURCE EFFICIENCY ON THIS PROTOTYPE. Do not claim compactness or total-resource parity. Before additional feature work, simplify or replace MR32's state/update algorithm and introduce equal-format full-state accounting plus stronger conventional recurrent/Bayesian controls.
